plotSections.title: The Spectral Door and Invisible Gerk
bullets: A strange spectral door is present aboard the boat, while Gerk is standing invisibly beside it and cannot move normally.
Sylan discovers Gerk by physically walking into him, then repeatedly interacts with and shakes the unseen Gerk while trying to understand the situation.
Gerk eventually gives up trying to remain standing and allows himself to fall to the floor; Sylan catches/supports his falling body before lowering him.
The spectral door continues hovering above Gerk as the party tries to communicate and determine what is happening.

plotSections.title: Attempts to Communicate with the Invisible Party Members
bullets: Sylan uses coins to create visible writing on the deck, spelling out a greeting to the others and attempting to communicate despite Gerk being unable to help.
Sylan later rearranges the coins to write Gerk's name with an arrow indicating where the invisible Gerk is, communicating that Gerk is in trouble.
Ord experiments with ways to reveal an invisible person, initially considering powder or dust before realizing he has a dragon vessel that can be used to apply liquid to himself.

plotSections.title: Ord's Oil Experiment
bullets: Ord pours olive oil over himself using his dragon vessel to test whether coating his body will reveal his position despite the unusual disappearance effect.
The experiment succeeds partially: an invisible Ord becomes detectable as a faint oil silhouette, with the oil visibly outlining his body despite making little to no normal splashing sound.
The party continues experimenting while the spectral door remains above Gerk and the nature of the invisibility/disappearance remains unexplained.

chronologicalEvents: Sylan investigates the strange door and discovers that an invisible Gerk is standing beside it.
Sylan hits the unseen Gerk in the head to confirm that someone is physically present.
Gerk attempts to deal with the strange force affecting him but cannot technically move normally; he eventually allows himself to fall to the floor.
Sylan supports Gerk's fall and lowers him to the deck.
Sylan uses coins to write a message on the deck so the others can communicate with him and locate Gerk.
Ord considers using powder or dust to reveal an invisible person, but abandons the idea after checking his inventory.
Ord remembers his dragon vessel and uses it to pour olive oil over himself.
The oil produces a faint visible silhouette of Ord, demonstrating that physical material can reveal the location of someone affected by the invisibility.
Sylan uses the coins to mark Gerk's location and indicate that Gerk is in trouble.
Sylan continues physically shaking and interacting with the invisible Gerk while the spectral door hovers above him.

notes: Gerk is affected by the strange invisibility/disappearance phenomenon and cannot be seen even though he remains physically present.
Gerk appears unable to move normally while affected, although the DM permits him to fall to the ground by giving up his attempt to remain standing.
Gerk remains physically tangible: Sylan can collide with, strike, support, and shake him despite being unable to see him.
A very shiny spectral door is hovering above Gerk while he is affected by the phenomenon.
personality: Gerk remains cooperative and eventually gives up struggling to remain upright when the situation prevents him from moving normally.
quotesThemes: The party is trying to physically interact with and locate Gerk despite his invisibility.
openQuestions: Why is Gerk invisible and unable to move normally?
What is the relationship between Gerk's condition and the spectral door hovering above him?

notes: Sylan discovers the invisible Gerk by walking around the spectral door and physically making contact with him.
Sylan experiments with physical interaction to determine Gerk's condition, including hitting and shaking him.
Sylan uses coins as a communication medium, creating visible messages on the deck and marking Gerk's location.
personality: Sylan responds to the unusual situation through hands-on experimentation and improvised communication.
quotesThemes: Using coins as temporary written communication when normal interaction with Gerk is impossible.

notes: Ord investigates whether a physical substance can reveal someone affected by the disappearance/invisibility effect.
Ord initially considers powder or dust but realizes he has a dragon vessel and instead uses olive oil.
The olive oil experiment produces a faint visible silhouette of Ord, showing that the phenomenon does not prevent physical substances from outlining an affected person.
personality: Ord approaches the strange phenomenon experimentally, trying to find a practical way to make invisible people detectable.
quotesThemes: Testing physical substances as a means of revealing otherwise invisible people.

notes: A spectral door appears aboard the boat and remains hovering above or near Gerk.
The door appears to be physically intangible or otherwise unusual, but its exact nature and purpose are not established in this chunk.
Sylan investigates the door by walking around it and discovers that Gerk is standing beside it rather than being part of the door itself.
quotesThemes: The spectral door is closely associated with the strange invisibility and movement restrictions affecting Gerk.
openQuestions: What is the spectral door and why did it appear?
Why is it hovering above Gerk?

notes: Ord has a dragon vessel in his inventory that he uses to pour olive oil over himself.
The vessel provides a practical way for Ord to coat himself in a liquid while investigating the invisibility phenomenon.

misTranscriptions.notes: The DM explicitly identifies the person as Gerk.
Likely ASR variation of Gerk during Gerk's dialogue.
The surrounding dialogue is explicitly about Gerk.
The DM asks how Sylan is interacting with Gerk immediately afterward.
Repeatedly appears when the DM describes Sylan.
Sylan is using coins to write a greeting; the transcript likely merged the greeting with Sylan's name.
Ord refers to something having disappeared rather than moved through the air; the exact intended word is unclear.
The surrounding discussion explicitly establishes that the ship has black powder/gunpowder.

openQuestions: Why is Gerk invisible and unable to move normally?
What is the spectral door and why is it associated with Gerk?
Can physical substances reliably reveal people affected by the disappearance/invisibility effect, or did the oil only reveal Ord's outline because of some special property?
Has this disappearance/invisibility phenomenon happened previously, as Ord suspects?

newTerms.name: Spectral Door
notes: A mysterious spectral door that appears aboard the boat and hovers near or above the invisible Gerk.

newTerms.name: Dragon Vessel
notes: An item in Ord's inventory that he uses to pour olive oil over himself during an experiment to reveal an invisible person.

newTerms.name: Oil Silhouette
notes: Physical oil can outline a person affected by the invisibility phenomenon, producing a faint visible silhouette without making normal splashing sounds.
